summary: This topic explains the concept of manual concessions, which are ad-hoc concessions given to students without predefined criteria, often at the discretion of the institute. It describes how to set up a 'Manual Concession' group to allow for flexible, on-the-fly concession application.
steps: When applying a manual concession to a student (typically from the student's fee demand or profile):
Manually enter the desired concession amount (the 'Flat 0' setup makes this field editable).
Enter relevant remarks for the concession.
Optionally, upload supporting documents (e.g., an application with principal's signature).
business_rules: Manual concessions are used when the amount and criteria are not predefined and vary per student.
The system will issue a warning if a concession is applied after fees have already been received for the affected installment.
important_notes: Setting up a 'Manual Concession' group with 'Flat' and '0' allows for flexible, ad-hoc concession amounts to be entered at the time of assignment.
This is useful for principal-approved or special case concessions.
The system provides a warning if a concession is applied to an amount that has already been received.
questions: What is a manual concession and when is it used?
How do I set up a 'Manual Concession' group in the system?
Can I enter any amount for a manual concession?
Can I upload documents for a manual concession?
What happens if I apply a manual concession after fees are paid?
